title: Tansy's Perfect Pet
markdown:
In Candlecrag, the air was not just cold. It sparkled. Tiny ice crystals danced like scattered diamonds and tickled every nose. Tansy, a goblin with ears as green and fresh as unfurling leaves, wiggled her own. Today felt like the perfect day for a pet. Not a skittery beetle. Not a grumpy toad. Tansy wanted a friend for big adventures, someone to whisper secrets with, maybe even share a cozy warm cave.

“Pip!” She spotted Pipkin the squirrel on a snow-laden pine branch. His tail, a fluffy exclamation point, twitched wildly.

“A pet! What kind of pet?” He squeaked, a furry streak tumbling down the tree. “A nut-gatherer? A tree-climber? A super-speedy acorn-hider, bushy-tailed one!” He zipped up and down a nearby branch and showered Tansy with glittering snow.

Tansy watched, a little sigh escaping. Pipkin was fast, yes, but too fast. Keeping up felt like trying to catch a runaway snowflake. Her leafy ears drooped a touch.

Further on, nestled in the deep crook of an ancient oak, sat Luna Bright. The owl’s feathers gleamed like a winter moon. Huge eyes twinkled wisely.

“Hoo-hoo, Tansy.” A rustle of dry leaves. “Seeking a friend for mountain quiet?”

“Yes, Luna.” She kicked a drift of snow. “But Pipkin said a speedy one. I need a friend I can actually walk with.”

Luna blinked. “A pet should be wise, my dear. A creature of the night, perhaps. One who watches and understands without needing to rush. Think of a little bat, or a shadow-kitten.”

Tansy imagined a shadow-kitten, all whispers and quiet paws. It sounded a bit too shadowy. And bats, with their darting flight, seemed a little too fluttery for a comfy companion.

Just then a puff of smoke, cinnamon and toasted hazelnuts, billowed from a nearby cave. Smolder the dragon emerged, scales the colour of a dying campfire. He was enormous, but his golden eyes held a warm amused spark.

“What troubles you, little goblin?” Friendly tumbling rocks.

“Oh, Smolder! I want a pet! Pipkin said fast. Luna said wise and shadowy. I don’t know what friend is right!”

Smolder puffed cinnamon smoke, swirling like a gentle cloud. “Nonsense!” The boom echoed. “A pet should be grand! Fierce! A guardian of your pebbles with a mighty roar!” Golden eyes glinted. “I suggest a baby griffin! Or perhaps a miniature lava salamander! Think of the warmth and protection on chilly nights!”

Tansy giggled. A lava salamander to warm her toes sounded lovely. A baby griffin sounded loud and prone to pouncing. Smolder always had grand impractical ideas for a small goblin.

She trudged home, snow crunching. The sparkling shelves that had seemed full of promise now felt too vast, too cold. So many creatures, and none quite right. She slumped near a large boulder, like a sleeping giant in a white blanket. A heavy feeling settled in her tummy. She was beginning to feel glum.

A tiny movement near the boulder’s base caught her eye. Tucked into a sheltered nook, hidden by a fluffy snowdrift, was a small fluffy creature. No bigger than Tansy’s paw. Fur the colour of fresh untouched snow. Two enormous bright blue eyes, like tiny pieces of summer sky, blinked slowly. It made a soft contented mew, a tiny crystal bell. It was not fast, or fierce, or even very wise. It was just soft. And warm. And very, very small.

A happy little shiver zipped through Tansy. This was it. This was the pet.

Very gently she scooped up the snow-white fluff. The creature nestled into her hands as if it belonged, purring a soft rumble that tickled her fingers. It felt like holding a tiny living snowball that had decided to be warm. She looked back at the snowy shelves, the white stretching all around. Not just cold and sparkly anymore. The colour of her new friend.

With the companion snuggled safely in a moss-lined pouch, purr against her chest, Tansy scampered happily toward home. The silent snowy landscape, once a place of searching, filled with the quiet joy of a purring friend. Every sparkling crystal became a tiny personal treasure. Pipkin, when she passed the pine, did a respectful loop in the air and did not shower her this time. Luna’s eyes, from the oak, approved without a lecture. Smolder’s cave sent one last cinnamon puff, which smelled, Tansy thought, a little like welcome.

She named nothing grand. The fluff did not need a roar. In the cozy cave, two leafy ears and two summer-sky eyes watched the ice crystals settle, and Candlecrag, for once, felt exactly the right size.
characters: Tansy (leaf-eared goblin of Candlecrag), Pipkin (speedy squirrel of the pines)
